column7: Run, fast stop, reset and coast stop bits; needs P1-12 = 4.
column15: bit 0 = Run/stop: 1 = run (enable), 0 = stop; bit 1 = Fast stop: 1 = stop using the 2nd deceleration ramp; bit 2 = Fault reset: 1 = reset trip; set back to 0 after the fault clears; bit 3 = Coast stop: 1 = coast to stop

column7: Frequency setpoint in 0.1 Hz (500 = 50.0 Hz); needs P1-12 = 4.
Accel/decel time 0-60000 = 0.00-600.00 s; used only when P5-07 = 1.
Low byte = status bits, high byte = fault code when tripped.
column15: bit 0 = 1 = running (enabled), 0 = stopped; bit 1 = 1 = tripped, 0 = healthy; bit 3 = 1 = inhibit (STO input open), 0 = ready (STO closed); bit 4 = 1 = maintenance time reached; bit 5 = 1 = standby (sleep) mode active; bit 6 = 1 = ready: mains on, no inhibit, no trip, enable input present; bit 8 = Bits 8-15 (upper byte): fault code number while tripped (50 = Modbus comms fault)
bit 0 = Digital input 1; bit 1 = Digital input 2; bit 2 = Digital input 3

column7: Measured DC bus voltage in whole volts.
x10 per the guide's example (500 = 50.0 Hz); rpm when P1-10 > 0.
Same format as P1-01; rpm when P1-10 > 0.
Action when the enable signal is removed.
column15: 0 = Ramp; 1 = Coast; 2 = Ramp, brake chopper enabled; 3 = Coast, brake chopper enabled; 4 = AC flux braking

column7: Motor nameplate voltage (back-EMF for PM motors).
0 = speeds shown in Hz; nameplate rpm switches to rpm.
Set 4 to control the drive over Modbus RTU.
column15: 0 = Terminal control; 1 = Keypad control, uni-directional; 2 = Keypad control, bi-directional; 3 = PID control; 4 = Fieldbus mode (Modbus RTU when no option module fitted); 5 = Slave mode; 6 = CANopen mode

column7: Digital input macro selection (see guide's P1-13 table).

column15: 0 = Trip and coast to stop; 1 = Ramp to stop then trip; 2 = Ramp to stop only (no trip); 3 = Run at preset speed 8
0 = Disabled (ramps from P1-03/P1-04); 1 = Enabled (ramps from fieldbus)
